Quest board 🧭 Full Season 4 quest board now live Growth / BD Marketing
37 quests across 7 categories — content, ecosystem projects, community building, regional & translation, support, official campaigns and referrals. Week-2 volume drivers: Share Your Cronos app Story (55), Translate Announcement (47), 📬 “Invites Are Rolling Out” quote tweet (47), Closed Beta Flex (42), Short-form app content (38), Ecosystem project text (36), Engage with app content (23), 🛡️ Chainalysis quote tweet (13).
Impact: the board is the steering wheel — every category now points at the Cronos app. Week 2 shows how fast it can be aimed: two flash-mission quote tweets on the waitlist invites and the Chainalysis coverage were spun up mid-week and drew 60 submissions between them.
Recap · Discord 🎙️ Ambassador Hour recap — Cronos app with Sam, Product team 🎧 recording Product Growth
Discord voice session · Wed Aug 5, 2026 · 9:00 PM GMT+8 · 31 registered
Sam took every hard question head-on. The through-line: the Cronos app is deliberately not a crypto app — social login instead of seed phrases, no blockchain jargon, and the on-chain wallet left untouched alongside a separate app wallet. The flagship is unified spot and perps on one screen with one slider. He was straight about the parts ambassadors get asked: perps route through Hyperliquid and spot through VVS today, with Cronos' own backend the goal; geo rules — not bugs — explain why people in the same region see different options; and the app freezing on close-position is not normal, with fixes landing across this sprint and next. Next up: prediction markets and sports in weeks, then a fund migration tool.
Impact: ambassadors left with quotable, first-hand answers to the five questions the community keeps asking — which is why they are now correcting the “spot goes through Hyperliquid too” misread in chats instead of routing it back to us. The session also produced new material for the social clip quest: the podcast with Alex (WolfSwap) and Smit.

💬 Ambassador sentiment Marketing

Discord ambassador chat · Aug 3 – 10 — a read on brand mood, not product feedback
Impact: a live pulse on how the app is landing with an influential, crypto-native audience — and an early read on where community questions are piling up. This week it doubled as the early-warning system on the DAT news.

🛠️ What users are telling Product Product

Everything below comes from closed-beta F&F testers only — the direct product-input pipe for R1
Impact: real testers surface what to fix and build next before wider launch — every item below feeds the R1 roadmap. F&F items sit alongside internal & ambassador reports in the full log (236 entries) in the Feedback & Bugbash Tracker →
💡 Top feature / UX asks56 from F&F
• Trailing stops, and TP/SL editable from the chart — two experienced traders, independently new · Aug 4–5
• Price alerts & notification control — price-movement alerts (the most-requested feature), plus liquidation warnings, market-open alerts and opt-in per type in the pipeline
• Sorting in Markets — can't order the list by price, change or volume 3 tracker rows · latest Aug 6
• A public Telegram channel for app and on-chain support — one open channel covering both the app and on-chain/DeFi questions, because Discord is seen as too restrictive; the first request for a public support surface rather than a feature new · Aug 11 · pending tracker row
• Clearer on-ramp deposit fees — flagged by Kwony Park, CDC Chief Strategy Officer new · Aug 4
• Already confirmed on the roadmap — pre-registered withdrawal addresses with a time-lock (a tester’s security suggestion, confirmed Aug 6, three weeks after it was raised), and shareable win/loss cards for social posting — a third and fourth tester asked for that on Aug 8 and Aug 10, and it is already logged P3 “already in roadmap” in roadmap ✓
• Account-level 2FA at login — a second factor to get into the app at all, not only at withdrawal, since assets are held inside it new · Aug 7
• The Onchain Wallet switch is awkward both ways — getting to OCW takes Profile > parameters every time; getting back sits next to “delete account” 3 reporters
• In-app chat, per asset or category — so traders can talk without leaving the app and newcomers have somewhere to ask; framed as a time-in-app driver, and the first request for an in-app social surface new · Aug 10
• A wider tradable universe — and pre-IPO access — more stocks, more cryptos and commodities such as copper (Aug 11), and from the same trader on Aug 12 a distinct ask for pre-IPO / pre-listing equity exposure, which he already gets elsewhere and frames as a time-boxed launch-marketing hook new · Aug 11–12 · tracker row 236
🐞 Notable bugs (P0/P1)19 from F&F
• The −50% stop-loss preset is rejected as “below liquidation” — at −50% the stop should sit above the liquidation price, so either the preset maths or the liquidation check is wrong; the reporter’s point is that the preset is pointless otherwise. Screenshot supplied new · Aug 11 · tracker row 235, logged Aug 12
• App freezes / screens won't load — a financial-loss risk: a tester couldn't close a profitable leveraged position. iOS and Android, escalated, owner assigned. Traced to region, not a stale session — repeatably works on a Brazil VPN and breaks without it. Still hits roughly one session in four, and a single log-out/log-in clears it. No dedicated Sprint 3 item — only P2 latency instrumentation. 11 users · 16 reports · 12 days
• Top-up / card / Apple & Google Pay failures — no bank-side alert; longest-running open item, with a third Google Pay reporter on Aug 5 and a further reporter on Aug 13 whose Apple Pay debit-card top-up failed on three consecutive attempts, using the card he had funded with before. Confirmed to him in-group as a known issue with a fix in the next app update, and he was pointed to the FAQ topic for the other known issues Onramper fix in Sprint 3
• Feed click-area too small — and buy/sell bubbles clutter the chart; the original reporter re-checked on the Aug 11 build and it is still reproducing 4 reports · re-checked Aug 11
• Leverage slider glitch while dragging — video supplied, acknowledged; the original reporter confirms it working after the latest update (Aug 11) 3 reporters reporter-confirmed fix ✓
• On-ramp certificate warning — fiat redirect warns of possible impersonation; security-facing Onramper replaces this flow in Sprint 3
• PnL figures disputed — don't match the venue's own API; moved to DM, unresolved
• Stop-loss won't drag past breakeven — forces the user to keep risk on a winner 2 reporters
• Short on CASHCAT will not open with a market order — limit and stop orders route fine, only market fails; surfaced, questioned and then confirmed by the testers themselves, and two testers have since reported market shorts opening normally, so it now reads as intermittent rather than standing. The team picked the thread up in-group on Aug 11. 2 reporters · intermittent · re-tested Aug 11
• “Realized” PnL on spot for a tester who never sold — about $13 shown as realized; may share a root cause with the older report that PnL calculation counts deposits new · Aug 11
✅ Latest reads (through Aug 13, 08:26 SGT) — quiet on new problems, busy on answers. Only one new report has come in since the Aug 12 build, and it is the longest-running item again: a tester’s Apple Pay debit-card top-up failed on three consecutive attempts on Aug 13, and the team answered him in the group the same morning — a known issue, with a fix in the next app update. The two items first raised on Aug 11 are now logged in the tracker: the −50% stop-loss preset bug as row 235, and the pre-IPO access ask (raised Aug 12) as row 236. Everything else stands where it did on Aug 12 — the leverage-slider fix is reporter-confirmed, the CASHCAT market short reads intermittent, the feed click-area is still reproducing on the Aug 11 build, and the freeze bug still hits roughly one session in four, cleared by a single log-out / log-in.
⚙️ Sprint 3 · app version v3.0.0 Build 3 · release date Aug 24, 2026 11 days out
What Sprint 3 answers from this list — and what it doesn’t. Shipping: the Onramper deposit integration (P0), the fix path for the longest-running item here — card / Apple Pay / Google Pay top-up failures and the on-ramp certificate warning — plus latency tracking (P2, latency first). Three further P0 buckets are open as post-launch feedback follow-ups for Portfolio, Perps / Spot and Discovery, which is where most of the asks above should land. Not scoped this sprint: the freeze / screens-won’t-load bug has no item of its own, CRO deposit is P3 tech-estimation only, and the OCW-switch work is deprioritised for lack of resources. The bulk of the sprint is Predictions — a surface the beta group has barely commented on. Confirmed to the group: on Aug 11 the team told the beta group that the next round of updates ships in about two weeks, which lines up with this release date — and on Aug 13 that same window was given to a reporter of the top-up failure as the fix ETA for that specific bug.

💬 How the launch is landing Marketing

Read through Aug 13 (08:26 SGT) from the closed beta group · brand-mood signal, not the product backlog
Impact: a live pulse on how R1 is received by an influential, crypto-native audience — useful for launch messaging & timing decisions.
🙂 Positive, testing patience
The app itself keeps winning people over — a tester who had never traded before said long and short were finally made simple to understand, and another demoed it to non-tester traders from a TradFi background who called it very easy to use, though they still want TradingView-grade charts before switching. What changed this week is the first open criticism of turnaround, not of the product: the tester who couldn't close a profitable position wrote that critical issues should take hours, not days.
🎓 "Long & short finally make sense" 👍 TradFi traders call it "very easy" ⚡ Instant fills 🧼 Clean, simple UI ✅ Smooth onboarding 🤝 Testers answering each other ⏱️ "Critical issues should take hours, not days" 📉 Charting still the blocker for pros 🗺️ First roadmap confirmation on a tester ask 🤝 Testers now policing off-topic threads 🌍 “90% of the app is restricted for US users” 🤫 ~21 joiners still silent 🛠️ Testers diagnosing bugs together 💬 “A live chat inside the app” 📱 “Cronos is my most-used app this week” 🔧 First reporter-confirmed fix 📋 Asks for a public bug-status list 🏦 “Pre-IPO access shouldn’t be difficult” 📅 Fix window shared in-group
🧠 Two audiences now share one group. The F&F base is highly crypto-native and technical; the waitlist cohort is not, and the newer voices are the ones praising how understandable the app is. The pro traders, meanwhile, are the ones setting the bar — trailing stops, inline order controls, real charts.
🙌 Acknowledging a report visibly changes the mood. Telling one reporter his issue was "in the pipeline" drew an immediate thank-you and pulled a second trader into the thread with better detail. The reverse is also true: the sharpest message this week came from someone waiting days without a status. Response speed, not fix speed, is what the group reacts to. The Aug 8 read bore that out: three older reports answered in one morning, including a roadmap confirmation on a tester’s own security idea — good material for launch comms, and the clearest counter yet to the "critical issues should take hours" criticism. On Aug 11 the team was active in the thread again — answering the standing “are all bugs solved?” question with a two-week update window, and replying in the CASHCAT thread. Aug 12–13 was the most responsive window of the beta so far: the support-channel ask, the tax-export ask, the tokenised-stock dividend question and the Apple Pay top-up failure were all answered in-group, the last of them with a fix ETA. A tester also answered the top-up report himself before the team did — the group is now carrying some of the triage.

🔒 Read this first

Confidential — internal Cronos use only. Do not share outside the team.
This is context and awareness, not answer copy. Nothing on this tab should be used directly in a reply to a user, quoted, screenshotted or paraphrased to anyone outside Cronos. It exists so that when a user raises something in the in-app CS channel you already know whether it is a known issue, where it sits with product, and who to route it to.
Where these reports come from. Internal Cronos team members and the closed beta testing group, reported through the Telegram group chat — not through Intercom. That means an item can appear here without any corresponding Intercom conversation, and the wording is a tester’s, not a customer’s.
Raising an issue. If a report has not come in through the Intercom messenger yet, strictly follow the Jira ticket flow to raise it. Do not treat presence on this tab as a substitute for a ticket, and do not raise duplicates against items already listed here.
How to read a row. Everything is on one line: the report as it was logged, the product team’s notes, severity (product’s internal priority, P0 highest), triage status, target release, and the owner PM to route to. A blank PM means none has been assigned on the tracker yet. Reporter identities, engineering owners and Jira links are excluded. Snapshot taken 13 Aug 2026, 08:26 SGT.
